subject: Waypoint: evidence allowance vs ongoing residency fee — pilot pricing options

Subject: Residency vs evidence cost for short pilot (SOW attached)

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for running the pilot demo last week. Procurement asked me to share the SOW and flag two questions up front so we can get a clean PO in place:

1) We have two internal options for handling compliance costs for the 3-month pilot: a one-time evidence/attestation allowance (single invoice) that covers SOC-2/Audit-log evidence collection + HSM attestation support, or
2) an ongoing residency fee (monthly) that covers data residency and audit log retention plus HSM seats.

For budgeting, they want a clear comparison of total cost over the 3-month pilot and the annualized cost if we convert to production. We also need to understand what credits, amortization, or rollback options Redwood would entertain if we decide not to go to production after the pilot.

I attached the SOW and our rough usage profile. Can you share your recommended commercial approach and a sample price table? If possible, can you also point to any precedent for a pilot-friendly credit treatment?

Thanks —
Katie

Hi Katie —

Appreciate the SOW and the clear framing. High level we typically offer two commercial patterns for pilot -> production paths, designed to make pilots low-friction while protecting the amortizable costs we incur for evidence and HSM on-boarding:

Option A — One-time Evidence Allowance + lower ongoing residency fee
- One invoice that covers evidence package creation (SOC/attestation artifacts), audit log packaging, and one HSM seat onboarding.
- Ongoing residency fee (monthly) set at a discounted pilot-rate; if you convert to production within 90 days we apply the allowance as a credit against the first 6 months of residency fees.

Option B — Monthly residency fee that includes evidence ops (no upfront invoice)
- Higher monthly rate during pilot (bundled) but no separate upfront charge. If you stop after pilot there is no refund, but we can do a one-time concession on final invoice if you commit to a future statement of work.

We prefer Option A for teams that are procurement-sensitive because it makes the pilot P&L line-item transparent and simpler to move to a PO. For Waypoint's SOW and expected scale (small pilot, light logs), I recommend Option A plus a rollback credit that reduces the residency bill by 50% for the first month if you cancel within 30 days — this is consistent with precedent we’ve offered for similar healthcare pilots.

I'll copy Aditya to propose a simple pricing table and Ben to flag any billing operational constraints. If that sounds good, we can produce a short amendment to the SOW showing both options.

Best,

Thanks for the context — I ran the numbers against Waypoint’s usage profile from the SOW. Below are two concrete sample tables you can share with procurement; these keep the math simple for PO creation. I’m keeping rounding conservative.

Option A (recommended) — One-time Evidence Allowance + discounted pilot residency
- Evidence allowance (one-time, invoiced up front): $28,500 — covers SOC evidence packaging, audit-log export mapping, HSM onboarding for 1 seat, and one-day onsite/remote attestation workshop.
- Pilot residency fee (monthly): $7,500/month (3 months total = $22,500)
- If converted to production within 90 days: apply evidence allowance as a credit across the first 6 months of residency ($4,750/month credit until consumed).
- Net pilot spend if converted = residency months after credit applied (example math depends on production scale).

Option B — Bundled monthly (no upfront)
- Bundled pilot rate: $13,000/month (includes evidence ops + HSM seat)
- 3 months = $39,000 total. No refundable credits.

Recommended framing for procurement: present Option A as pilot-friendly (lower monthly line) and include a simple rollback clause: if you cancel before the 30 day mark into the pilot we invoice 50% of the first month residency fee and waive remaining months; if you cancel after 30 days but before 90 days we invoice full pilot residency months and retain the evidence allowance with no extra penalty.

Attachments: I’m attaching a quick resid-fee model and a one-page amendment template we can use for the PO.

Aditya

- Credit scope: confirmed — credit only applies to recurring residency fees; usage-based charges (per-token, embeddings) are separate and not eligible for credit. We’ll add explicit language in the amendment.
- 90-day window: measured from pilot start date (first API call / activation date), but we’ll include an explicit date field in the amendment to avoid ambiguity.
